check_color_availability.description: Check which of up to 100 colors are still unnamed on OpenColors, in one request. Each color comes back as available or already named, with the name and owner when it is taken, and the two lists are summarised so a step can branch on the counts or take the available hexes straight into the next step.
check_color_availability.name: check_color_availability

parameters.description: The colors to check, one per entry, in any hex spelling. Up to 100 at a time; a repeat is checked once. A single text of colors separated by commas works too.
parameters.name: hexes

color_count.description: How many colors were answered for.

colors.description: Each color OpenColors answered for, in the order asked.

available.description: True when nobody has named the color yet.

hex_int.description: The color as a whole number: the hex read in base 16, which is how OpenColors' bulk check spells it.

requested_count.description: How many different colors were asked about.

check_contrast.description: Check a color's WCAG 2.1 contrast against a white and a black background: the ratio on each, whether it passes AA and AAA for small text, large text and UI components, which of the two it reads best on, and the text color OpenColors recommends for anything written on top of it. check_service_status.description: Check whether OpenColors is answering, how quickly, and what it reports about itself: its own status, the state of its database and its version. This is the one action that reports a problem as a value instead of failing the step, so a workflow can decide what to do about it.

get_brand.description: Get one brand's official palette by name. The service only searches, so the name is searched for and matched here: an exact name or slug always wins, and failing that a partial name resolves when it lands on a single brand, so 'spotify' and 'the Spotify brand' both work. A name matching two brands is reported with both rather than guessed between.

description: Look up any color on OpenColors, the free keyless color data API. Turn a hex code into RGB, HSL, HSV and CMYK, find out whether someone has named it and who, or get the nearest named color and how far off it is. Check a color's WCAG 2.1 contrast against white and black, see it as people with each kind of color blindness do, check which of up to a hundred colors are still unnamed in one request, search the colors people have named or list the newest, and pull the official palettes of more than 600 brands, from Spotify's green to Netflix's red.
